basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 12.' and it opens 'VERS. 12.-- Dixitque Adam: Mulier quam dedisti sociam, dedit mihi de ligno, et comedi.'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 12.-- Dixitque Adam: Mulier quam dedisti sociam, dedit mihi de ligno, et comedi. Heu, ubi peccatum finem habere debuit, ibi augmentum coepit! | Non enim culpam ad se retulit, sed quodam modo ad mulierem, quam Dominus dederat, et reatum suum oblique in Auctorem redegit [ Z., rediit], qui ei talem sociam dederat, unde occasio peccati esset. Unde nunc quoque humani generis rami ex hac adhuc radice amaritudinem trahunt, et cum de vitio suo quisque arguitur, sub defensionum umbra, quasi sub quaedam se arborum folia abscondit. In qua videlicet occultatione non se Domino, sed Dominum abscondit sibi.
